body:
The literary awakening of the 19th century

The middle of the 19th century marked a major transformation in Gujarati literature. English education, printing, newspapers and social reform debates encouraged writers to address subjects beyond traditional religious narratives.

This period is known as Sudharak Yug, the Age of Reform, or Narmad Yug. Literature increasingly discussed education, social customs, individual freedom, women's condition and regional identity. Poetry remained important, but essays, dictionaries, autobiographies, novels and social plays acquired greater prominence.

Narmad

Narmad was the literary name of Narmadashankar Lalshankar Dave (1833–1886). Associated with Surat, he was a poet, essayist, lexicographer and social reformer who played a foundational role in modern Gujarati literature.

His writings expressed reformist ideas, personal experience, patriotism and pride in Gujarati identity. He helped broaden the subject matter of Gujarati poetry beyond its predominantly devotional medieval tradition.

Principal works and contributions

WorkImportance
Jai Jai Garvi GujaratCelebrated poem expressing Gujarati regional identity
Mari HakikatPioneering Gujarati autobiography, written in 1866
NarmakoshPioneering monolingual Gujarati dictionary, completed in published form in 1873
NarmagadyaCollection of prose writings
NarmakavitaCollection of poetic compositions
DandiyoReform-oriented periodical started in 1864

Mari Hakikat is generally regarded as the first Gujarati autobiography. It was written in 1866 but published posthumously. The year of composition should therefore not be confused with its publication year.

Narmakosh is conventionally recognized as the first major monolingual Gujarati dictionary. Earlier Gujarati-English glossaries existed, so it should not be described as the first dictionary of every kind involving Gujarati.

Dalpatram

Dalpatram Dahyabhai Travadi (1820–1898) was another pioneering poet and reform-oriented writer. His literature addressed social customs and moral behaviour while retaining a stronger connection with established poetic traditions.

Dalpatram worked with the Gujarat Vernacular Society, established in Ahmedabad in 1848 through the initiative of Alexander Kinloch Forbes. The society encouraged Gujarati literature, education and publication.

  • Farbas Virah: An elegiac poem expressing grief over the death of Forbes.
  • Mithyabhiman: A social comedy criticizing pride, pretence and hypocrisy.
  • Lakshmi: An early Gujarati play.
  • Dalpat Kavya: A collection of Dalpatram's poetic works.

Dalpatram assisted Forbes in collecting historical and literary material. However, Ras Mala was authored by Alexander Kinloch Forbes, not by Dalpatram.

Nandshankar Mehta and the first original Gujarati novel

Nandshankar Tuljashankar Mehta wrote Karan Ghelo, published in 1866. It is generally recognized as the first original Gujarati novel and is a historical narrative concerning Karna Vaghela, the last ruler of Gujarat's Vaghela dynasty.

Prelims focus

  • Narmad: Narmadashankar Lalshankar Dave.
  • Mari Hakikat: First Gujarati autobiography, written in 1866.
  • Narmakosh: Monolingual Gujarati dictionary, 1873.
  • Dalpatram: Farbas Virah and Mithyabhiman.
  • Karan Ghelo: Nandshankar Mehta, 1866.
  • Trap: Ras Mala was authored by Alexander Kinloch Forbes; Dalpatram assisted his research.

[References: Gujarati Vishwakosh, entries Narmad, Kavi Dalpatram, Mithyabhiman, Kosh Sahitya, Navalkatha and Gujarat: Gujarati Language and Literature; NCERT, India and the Contemporary World II, Class 10, Print Culture and the Modern World, sections on print in India. Online sources consulted 26 November 2026.]

title: Sudharak Yug: Narmad, Dalpatram and the Rise of Modern Gujarati Prose

body:
Characteristics of the scholarly period

The Pandit Yug, also called Sakshar Yug or Govardhan Yug, developed approximately between 1885 and 1915. Its writers were influenced by Sanskrit literature, Indian philosophy, classical learning and Western literary and educational traditions.

Whereas the preceding Sudharak Yug concentrated strongly on social reform, the Pandit Yug also examined cultural identity, moral philosophy, individual emotions and the relationship between Indian and Western ideas. Literary expression became more scholarly and developed through novels, lyric poetry, narrative poems and essays.

Govardhanram Tripathi

Govardhanram Madhavram Tripathi was a leading novelist of the Pandit Yug. His major work, Saraswatichandra, was published in 4 parts between 1887 and 1901.

The novel examines personal relationships, family duties, social customs, moral responsibilities, administration and the condition of Indian society. It is much broader than a romantic narrative between its principal characters.

Important poets and their literary identities

AuthorLiterary namePrincipal works
Manishankar Ratnaji BhattKantPurvalap, Vasant Vijay, Devayani
Sursinhji Takhtasinhji GohilKalapiKalapino Kekarav
Balwantrai Kalyanrai ThakoreSeheniBhanakar, Arohan
Narsinhrao Bholanath DivetiaJnanbalKusumamala, Hridayavina
Nhanalal Dalpatram KaviNhanalalVasantotsav, Kurukshetra, Chitradarshan

Kant and Kalapi

Kant was particularly important for the development of the khandakavya, a sustained poem centred on a particular episode or experience. His major poetry collection, Purvalap, appeared in 1923 and includes compositions such as Vasant Vijay and Devayani.

Kalapi was the literary name of Sursinhji Takhtasinhji Gohil, the ruler of Lathi in Saurashtra. His poetry is remembered for personal emotions, love, nature and romantic longing. His major collection is Kalapino Kekarav.

Nhanalal and Balwantrai Thakore

Nhanalal was the son of the reform-era poet Dalpatram. His work belongs primarily to the scholarly and romantic poetic tradition associated with the Pandit Yug. His works include Vasantotsav and Kurukshetra.

Balwantrai Thakore contributed to the development of reflective and intellectually oriented Gujarati poetry. His major poetic works include Bhanakar and Arohan.

Other significant writers

  • Manilal Nabhubhai Dwivedi: Associated with philosophical writing, Indian intellectual traditions and the Pandit Yug.
  • Ramanbhai Mahipatram Nilkanth: Author of the satirical novel Bhadrambhadra and the play Raino Parvat.
  • Anandshankar Dhruv: A prominent scholar and writer associated with philosophical and cultural reflection.

Prelims focus

  • Saraswatichandra: Govardhanram Tripathi, 4 parts, 1887–1901.
  • Kant: Manishankar Ratnaji Bhatt; Purvalap.
  • Kalapi: Sursinhji Takhtasinhji Gohil; Lathi.
  • Kusumamala: Narsinhrao Divetia.
  • Bhanakar: Balwantrai Thakore.
  • Trap: Dalpatram belongs to the Reform period, while his son Nhanalal is primarily associated with the Pandit period.

[References: IGNOU, Poetry, Unit 6, Section 6.2, p. 122; Gujarati Vishwakosh, entries Kant, Kalapi, Narsinhrao Divetia, Saraswatichandra and Gujarat: Gujarati Language and Literature; INFLIBNET e-PG Pathshala, Indian Literary Criticism and Theory, Chapter 30, History of Gujarati Literature. Online sources consulted 26 November 2026.]

pictures.caption: Dalpatram and Nhanalal belong to different literary generations.

title: Pandit Yug: Scholars, Novelists and Poets

body:
The Gandhian influence on literature

The emergence of Mahatma Gandhi as a major leader of India's freedom struggle profoundly influenced Gujarati literature. His return to India from South Africa in 1915 provides a conventional starting point for the Gandhi Yug.

Literature increasingly addressed truth, non-violence, social equality, village life, national freedom and the moral responsibilities of individuals. Compared with the heavily scholarly tendencies of the Pandit Yug, Gandhian writing generally preferred a simpler and more accessible literary language.

Not every writer of this period followed Gandhian philosophy in the same way. Historical novels, romantic short stories, folklore and other literary interests continued to flourish alongside nationalist literature.

Mahatma Gandhi as a Gujarati author

Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi used Gujarati prose to communicate political, ethical and social ideas to ordinary readers. Several of his important writings were originally composed in Gujarati and subsequently translated into other languages.

Major works

WorkPrincipal subject
Hind SwarajSelf-rule and criticism of modern civilization
Satya na PrayogoAutobiographical account of experiments with truth
Dakshin Afrikana Satyagrahano ItihasHistory of the Satyagraha movement in South Africa
Anasakti YogaGujarati rendering and interpretation of the Bhagavad Gita emphasizing non-attachment

Hind Swaraj was originally written in Gujarati in 1909. Its English version, Indian Home Rule, appeared in 1910.

Gandhi's autobiography, commonly known in Gujarati as Satya na Prayogo, was serialized in the Gujarati journal Navajivan between 1925 and 1929. Mahadev Desai translated it into English as An Autobiography or The Story of My Experiments with Truth.

Gandhian journalism

Gandhi used newspapers and journals to communicate directly with the public. Important publications associated with his work include:

  • Indian Opinion: Associated with his public activities in South Africa.
  • Navajivan: An important Gujarati publication associated with Gandhi.
  • Young India: An English-language publication used by Gandhi.
  • Harijan: Associated with Gandhi's campaign against untouchability and his constructive programme.
  • Harijan Bandhu: A Gujarati publication associated with his social reform campaigns.

Mahadev Desai

Mahadev Desai, Gandhi's secretary and close associate, was an important writer, translator and diarist. His writings provide an extensive record of Gandhi's activities and intellectual life.

Mahadevbhaini Diary is associated with Mahadev Desai. It received the Sahitya Akademi Award for Gujarati in 1955, posthumously.

Narmad's Mari Hakikat is the pioneering Gujarati autobiography written in 1866. Gandhi's autobiography, Satya na Prayogo, is a later work of the Gandhian period. Both are autobiographies, but their authors and historical contexts differ.

Prelims focus

  • Hind Swaraj: Originally written in Gujarati in 1909.
  • Indian Home Rule: English version of Hind Swaraj, 1910.
  • Satya na Prayogo: Serialized in Navajivan between 1925 and 1929.
  • Mahadev Desai: English translator of Gandhi's autobiography.
  • Anasakti Yoga: Gandhi's Gujarati rendering of the Bhagavad Gita.

[References: Ministry of Culture, Press Information Bureau, Remembering Bapu: Gandhi Heritage Portal, 1 October 2013, sections Key Texts and Journals; IGNOU, Poetry, Unit 6, Section 6.2, p. 122; Sahitya Akademi, Akademi Awards, Gujarati award entry for 1955. Online sources consulted 26 November 2026.]

pictures.caption: Original Gujarati writings and their English versions.

title: Gandhi Yug: Mahatma Gandhi, Nationalism and Literary Change

body:
Kanhaiyalal Maneklal Munshi

K. M. Munshi was a prominent Gujarati novelist, public figure and founder of Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan. He is particularly remembered for historical fiction that presents the political and cultural history of Gujarat through literary narratives.

The Patan historical trilogy

  1. Patan ni Prabhuta
  2. Gujarat no Nath
  3. Rajadhiraj

These historical novels are associated with medieval Gujarat and the Chaulukya or Solanki period. Munshi's other prominent works include Prithvi Vallabh and Jai Somnath.

Jhaverchand Meghani

Jhaverchand Meghani was a major collector and writer of Gujarati folk literature, as well as a poet and novelist. He is popularly remembered by the honorific Rashtriya Shayar, meaning national poet.

Meghani collected and preserved oral narratives, songs and traditions from Saurashtra, making this regional cultural heritage accessible through published literature.

  • Saurashtrani Rasdhar: A major collection of folk narratives from Saurashtra.
  • Sorathi Baharvatiya: Narratives associated with the outlaws and heroic traditions of Sorath.
  • Sindhudo: A collection of patriotic compositions associated with the freedom struggle.
  • Chhello Katoro: A celebrated poem addressed to Gandhi in connection with his journey to the Round Table Conference.

Dhumketu

Dhumketu was the pen name of Gaurishankar Govardhanram Joshi. He was a pioneering figure in the development of the modern Gujarati short story.

His collection Tankha, whose first volume appeared in 1926, occupies an important place in Gujarati short fiction. He wrote stories concerning ordinary people, human relationships, emotional suffering and social conditions. His celebrated story Post Office is an example of his emphasis on human feeling.

Ramnarayan Vishwanath Pathak

Ramnarayan Vishwanath Pathak was a versatile Gujarati writer who used different literary names for different kinds of writing.

Pen namePrincipal association
DwirefShort stories
SheshPoetry
SwairvihariEssays and reflective prose

Dwirefni Vato is associated with Pathak's short fiction. Dwiref, Shesh and Swairvihari are literary names of the same individual, not separate authors.

Other important literary figures

  • Snehrashmi: Pen name of Jhinabhai Ratanji Desai, a poet, educator and author of Gata Asopalav and Antarpat.
  • Ramanlal Vasantlal Desai: Novelist associated with Gandhian social concerns. His works include Gramalakshmi, Divyachakshu and Bharelo Agni.
  • Kakasaheb Kalelkar: Gandhian writer associated with essays, travel writing and works such as Jeevan-Vyavastha.

Prelims focus

  • K. M. Munshi: Patan ni Prabhuta, Gujarat no Nath and Rajadhiraj.
  • Jhaverchand Meghani: Saurashtrani Rasdhar and Rashtriya Shayar.
  • Dhumketu: Gaurishankar Govardhanram Joshi; Tankha.
  • Dwiref, Shesh and Swairvihari: Ramnarayan Vishwanath Pathak.
  • Snehrashmi: Jhinabhai Ratanji Desai.
  • Gramalakshmi: Ramanlal Vasantlal Desai.

[References: Gujarati Vishwakosh, entries Ramnarayan Vishwanath Pathak, Snehrashmi, Navalkatha and Gujarat: Gujarati Language and Literature; Maharashtra State Gazetteers, Language and Literature, section on Gujarati literature; Indian Express, How Dhumketu transformed Gujarati literature with his short stories, February 2021; Sahitya Akademi, Gujarati award entries. Online sources consulted 26 November 2026.]
